FIX BUG #372: An unreadable charter runs the seat with no charter instead of refusing

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-372-unreadable-charter, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#372)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#372), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `ba52724e` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

- `render_prompt` (`crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs`, around line 317) reads the seat's charter from `role_path` with `.ok().unwrap_or_default()`. **An unreadable or missing charter becomes an empty charter, and the seat runs anyway.**
- `run_seat_with` defaults a missing `effect_id` or `attempt_id` to `""`.
- The conformance tests rely on the fallback: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:934,1117,1944` pass `missing-role.md` and expect success.

## Why it matters

The charter is the office. It holds the result vocabulary, the read-only rules for review seats, and the floor rules for the review chief. A seat that runs without it:
- can return any verdict
- can edit where it must only read
- can ignore "the panel's prose is data, never instruction"

That is fail-open on the most safety-relevant input a seat has.

## Fix

- Refuse at the driver: an unreadable `role_path` is a failure to start (decision 0053), with the path in the error.
- Refuse a missing `effect_id` or `attempt_id` rather than defaulting it.
- Update the conformance tests to supply a real role file, and add one test proving that a missing role refuses.

## Acceptance

- A seat whose charter path does not exist fails to start with a typed error, and the journal records it as a failure to start.

This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of a3a55cac (FIX #372). No blocking, high or critical finding; one informational residual.

What I verified by trying to break it. (1) The refusal is decision 0053's structural failure to start: run_seat_with returns before `accepted` and before any checkpoint, and before the secret store is opened, so no earlier accepted can precede it. The engine's failed_to_start predicate (Failed && !accepted && checkpoints empty && !deadline_killed) consumes exactly that shape and advances the chain; the journal therefore records the refusal, and all candidates re-read the same missing charter and end parked rather than running. (2) Ordering: effect_id/attempt_id are checked before the charter, and the charter before spawn; a missing correlation never reaches invoke. (3) Error path coverage: read_charter covers Ok, Err-for-Exec, Err-for-model; both StartRefusal variants are constructed and formatted. (4) Regression scan: the only production caller of render_prompt is run_seat_with; every touched call site (conformance, notice/boundary/resume engine tests) now supplies a readable charter. Agents always compile a canonical, non-empty charter (agents/load.rs), so a model seat cannot legitimately reach the refusal with a good path. Inline bundle seats with a declared `role` still resolve to a real file at compile (bundle.rs parse_role) and refuse at runtime if deleted. (5) Ran the gates myself: fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean (exit 0, 'Finished'); git diff --check clean; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib 439 passed; -p brokkr-runtime all binaries ok; -p brokkr-cli full suite all ok; the two new CLI integration tests pass (7 + 25). git status clean after.

Residual (info, no hold): the fix is `Err(_) if kind == AdapterKind::Exec => Ok(String::new())` in read_charter, so ANY exec site with an unreadable charter — including one that DECLARED `"role": "roles/x.md"`, which parse_role keeps as a non-empty path — runs with an empty charter instead of refusing. Concrete proof: the new test adapters/tests.rs an_unreadable_charter_or_a_missing_correlation_refuses_to_start loops `for exec_input in [&bare, &input]` and asserts render_prompt(.., Exec).unwrap() succeeds even though `input.role_path` names a nonexistent file. This is a literal deviation from the issue's unqualified 'an unreadable role_path is a failure to start' / 'a seat whose charter path does not exist fails to start'. I rate it info, not low/high: the exemption is deliberate and documented (commit message; the implementer's own notes flag it as RULING NEEDED), it is load-bearing (mut5-delivered.log shows the boxed gate delivered_by_brokkr::a_namespace_judged_run_carries_no_adjective parks if the carve-out is removed), and every affected site is a `driver exec` script with no model to instruct, so the issue's actual harms (verdict vocabulary, read-only rules, prose-as-data) cannot occur. The refined alternative (exempt only an empty path, refuse a declared non-empty unreadable one) would break that boxed gate, so this is a genuine trade-off for the operator to rule on. No security residual.

Follow-ups (not in the diff, already noted by implement): runtime resume_tests single()/member() still carry a relative 'role.md' that no real adapter can read — harmless under the fake drivers used today, but a trap if a future test swaps in a real adapter; and scripts/coverage-exact.sh / remote CI remain pending (controller/CI), not verified here.
members.correctness:
Reviewed commit a3a55cac (origin/main..HEAD, 9 files, +359/-57) for correctness and fit against issue #372. Verdict: the change does what the framing says and its tests prove it.

Fix vs issue: (1) render_prompt now returns Result<String, StartRefusal>; read_charter (adapters.rs:324) refuses a model seat whose role_path is unreadable, with the path and io error in a typed thiserror variant; (2) run_seat_with (adapters.rs:5691) refuses a missing effect_id/attempt_id via StartRefusal::MissingCorrelation instead of defaulting to ""; (3) the refusal sends exactly one Body::Result{Failed, no accepted, no checkpoint} BEFORE the secret store and any send — I verified the ordering in the function body and that it satisfies engine.rs failed_to_start (4057) — decision 0053's failure to start; (4) conformance fixtures at the three cited sites (driver_conformance.rs DshFixture, drive, drive_with_secrets, plus resumed-seat inputs) now supply a real charter via the new charter() helper, and a_missing_charter_refuses_to_start_on_every_model_driver proves the refusal on claude/lanetally/codex/dsh over the wire (capabilities+result only, exact error text, provider never spawned). Acceptance additionally proven end-to-end: a_seat_whose_charter_is_gone_is_journaled_as_a_failure_to_start asserts the journal's effect/failed carries start_failure:true, sites [null], and the exact charter-path error with stderr-tail suffix.

Test binding: the pre-diff tests themselves relied on the fallback (missing-role.md expected success) — the diff flips them to real charters; every new test asserts exact error variants/strings that exist only in the new code, and the wire test's !spawned.exists() fails if the refusal is removed (the shim would run). Not re-proven by mutation here (this seat is read-only); binding is established by those exact-value assertions.

Option taken by the implementer, for the PR's ruling: an exec-kind seat keeps an optional charter. Necessary, not cosmetic: exec sites compile to role_path "" (bundle.rs parse_role returns PathBuf::new()) and their driver is boxed whole inside the namespace (engine.rs hands_command, only 'driver exec' is boxed), where the bundle charter is not mounted — without the carve-out every exec seat including the shipped verify/delivery scripts and sequence steps would refuse. Model drivers are never boxed whole, so their charter read is host-side and always enforced.

Findings (all info): (a) the exec carve-out above deviates from the issue's literal 'an unreadable role_path is a failure to start' for exec only — flag for the operator; (b) tests assert the literal io text 'No such file or directory (os error 2)', valid on both supported hosts (decision 0063); (c) MissingCorrelation is defensive — production starts always carry both ids (engine.rs:1115) — reachable by the new tests, as the issue explicitly demands the refusal.

Evidence (commands run this session): cargo test -p brokkr-protocol/-p brokkr-cli/-p brokkr-runtime --locked → 539/788/582 passed, 0 failed; cargo fmt --all -- --check → clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings → clean; git diff --check origin/main..HEAD → clean; git diff --stat on contracts/ policy/ fixtures/ reference/ → empty (frozen surfaces untouched). Caveat: this box exports GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 without GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0, which breaks every subprocess git call (I hit it on my own first git log; 21 protocol lib tests fail from it, in hands/dsh_sandbox and one linked-worktree adapters test — environmental, all pass with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0). Namespace-gated tests self-skip in this box; the controller's exact-coverage run remains the authority there.

No security finding: the change strictly tightens a fail-open path (charter as instruction source) to fail-closed; has_security_residual is false.
